brief: Goldman's Wednesday cross-asset recap: a hotter-than-expected September core CPI print (33bps vs 20bps consensus) lifted Fed hike odds (as high as 35% for October, 87% for December intraday) and triggered a broad risk-off session. Equities fell broadly, with the S&P posting its first 1%+ daily move in 53 days (SPX -111bps, NDX -202bps, RTY -193bps); tech and AI-linked names led losses (GS NeoClouds basket -10.93%, Quantum Computing index -7.14%) while defensive sectors (Healthcare, Staples, Energy) and a defensive basket outperformed as investors rotated to safety and bought Treasuries. Rates sold off sharply right after the print before paring back to close roughly flat, with the curve flattening modestly. Credit widened on AI-linked financing stress, with Oracle CDS, CoreWeave bonds, and datacenter spreads underperforming alongside broader IG/HY decompression. The dollar strengthened as EUR broke below 1.1190/1.1200 support toward 1.1000, with the note flagging risk that a US slowdown may not arrive in time to help Europe. Goldman previews Thursday's retail sales, PPI, and jobless claims data, mostly tracking consensus.
